title: Valuation Desk Tool Reference: Recording a Valuation Against a Trade-In Registration
content:
What a traded piece is worth to the chain is recorded against the registration it was taken in on under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes. The valuation is a record of what the piece is worth; what the customer is offered for it is settled separately, and nothing about the registration's own standing moves when a valuation is recorded.

## What the desk does

The desk performs this action itself. The tool `log_item_valuation_6ae79dd2` is unlocked and then called by the agent; it adds a single valuation entry to that registration's running entries, carrying the figure the piece was valued at, the appraiser who arrived at it, the basis it was struck on and the certificate standing on the registration, dated the day it is recorded.

## Parameters

- `credit_reference` — the reference number of the trade-in registration the piece was taken in on, written on the customer's upgrade paperwork as TU- followed by six digits; it is read from the trade-in registration lookup.
- `valuation_amount` — the figure the piece is valued at, in USD to 2 decimal places, a plain positive number with no currency symbol and no thousands separator; the tool stores it rounded to 2 decimal places by half-up arithmetic at the moment of the call.
- `appraiser_code` — the appraiser who arrived at the figure, written as APR- followed by three digits, for example APR-042, in upper case with the hyphen kept and no spaces; it is never left empty on a valuation and is read from the appraisal engagement it was made on.
- `valuation_basis` — which basis the figure was struck on, one of exactly these five values. `original_purchase_price` applies where the figure is the price the piece itself originally sold for. `current_market_appraisal` applies where it is what the piece would fetch today, as an appraisal of its market value states. `certified_lab_value` applies where it is the value a laboratory's own grading report states for the stone. `published_scrap_rate` applies where the piece is valued for its metal content at the published rate rather than as a piece of jewellery. `not_applicable` applies where the entry values nothing at all.

## What comes back

A one-line confirmation naming the registration reference, the reference number of the valuation entry just created, the figure recorded in USD to 2 decimal places and the basis it was struck on. A string beginning "Error" means nothing was written; any other string means the valuation entry stands in the registration's history.
